body.statement: For \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{joint}}(P)\), conditional on proving \(\mathrm{oeq:score-lifting-completeness}\), the observed joint-bridge functional \(\theta\) is pathwise differentiable if and only if \(\Phi_P\neq\varnothing\). Whenever this holds, every gradient lies in \(\mathcal A_P\) and \[\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}=\phi_0-\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\varphi\in\mathcal A_P}E[\varphi^2],\qquad V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)=\inf_{\varphi\in\mathcal A_P}E[\varphi^2].\] The claim is not unconditional: the projection becomes the canonical gradient only after the reverse score-lifting inclusion is established.
body.justification: The Hilbert projection and complete gradient-affine-space calculation are proved once tangent equality and bridge-score pathwise validity are available.
body.gap: Neither reverse score lifting nor unbounded-product bridge-score validity, including the claimed necessity of \(\Phi_P\ne\varnothing\), follows from the frozen assumptions.
body.consumer: Analysts must use the unconditional positive finite results or state both missing premises explicitly.

obligation.what_is_open: Prove bridge-score pathwise validity and the claimed pathwise-differentiability if-and-only-if statement on the unbounded existence-only chart, in addition to resolving reverse score lifting.
obligation.obstruction: Separate square integrability of the bridges and outcome does not control the products required to differentiate a bridge score along every DQM path. Operator continuity has no first-order modulus, so continuity of nearby minimum-norm representatives does not make the exact doubly robust product remainder little-o of the path parameter. Pathwise differentiability also does not presently imply that a single bridge-pair score belongs to square-integrable space.
obligation.attempted: I used the exact nearby-law doubly robust remainder and continuous pseudoinverse/kernel perturbation. The remainder is a product of a nearby primal and dual change; the assumptions make those changes continuous but do not provide the rate or product integrability needed after division by the path parameter. The remaining Hilbert projection argument was completed conditionally and is recorded below.
obligation.partial_result:
The Hilbert-space conclusion is complete under the two missing analytic premises. Namely, suppose that
\(\mathcal T_P=\mathcal C_P^\perp\) and that some
\(\phi_0\in\Phi_P\) represents the derivative of \(\theta\) along every actual path score:
\[
\dot\theta_P(s)=E[\phi_0s],\qquad s\in\dot{\mathcal P}_P.
\]
By the proved normal--affine identity and closedness of \(\mathcal C_P\),
\[
\mathcal A_P=\phi_0+\mathcal C_P.
\]
The projection theorem then gives the unique minimum-norm point
\[
\phi_*=\phi_0-\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0,
\qquad
\phi_*\perp\mathcal C_P,
\qquad
\phi_*\in\mathcal C_P^\perp=\mathcal T_P.
\]
For every \(s\in\mathcal T_P\),
\[
E[\phi_*s]
=E[\phi_0s]-E[(\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0)s]
=\dot\theta_P(s),
\]
so \(\phi_*\) is the canonical gradient. If \(g\) is any other gradient, then
\(E[(g-\phi_0)s]=0\) for every \(s\in\mathcal T_P\), whence
\(g-\phi_0\in\mathcal T_P^\perp=\mathcal C_P\). Conversely, adding any element of \(\mathcal C_P\) to \(\phi_0\) preserves the derivative representation. Thus the complete gradient set is
\(\phi_0+\mathcal C_P=\mathcal A_P\), and
\[
V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)=\|\phi_*\|_2^2
=\inf_{\varphi\in\mathcal A_P}E[\varphi^2].
\]
What is not derived from the frozen assumptions is the premise that a square-integrable bridge score represents every path derivative, nor the converse assertion that pathwise differentiability forces \(\Phi_P\ne\varnothing\).
